items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: that’s some rare film of Wardell Gray that rarely do you get a chance to see Wardell Gray on film.

ctx.x: But they let him stay in the film?

But in the south they did a lot of pairing of films that had black and whites. So you not only had darkened faces, there were sometimes Ellington and members of Ellington’s band were removed. I think “Check and Double Check” was an example of the blackening of faces also which was one of the first feature films where an African American musical group appeared. But I did read in one of the Basie books that for certain purposes, the sound of Buddy DeFranco was removed and replaced with Marshall Royal on the film…
Yeah. He died fairly young, didn’t he?
